label: RoboCat
original_allegation: "success-filter" is wrong. RoboCat does not filter self-generated data by success. Failed episodes are kept and relabelled with hindsight goals. Learned success detectors are used only to pick semantically-equivalent goal images for successful episodes, and to decide resets. "Fleet-scale" is hype-leaning wording that the paper does not use.
evidence: Section 2.1 retains unsuccessful episodes with hindsight goals; Section 2.1.2 uses 100–1000 demonstrations then self-generated trajectories. The architecture section specifies a 1.18B transformer.
applied_changes: {"one_line": "Self-improvement loop for a 1.18B visual-goal-conditioned transformer: fine-tune on 100-1000 demonstrations, collect new robot trajectories, hindsight-relabel goals including failed episodes, and retrain the generalist."}

label: iRe-VLA
original_allegation: "PPO on a small head" is not supported. The paper never says its Stage-1 RL uses PPO. PPO (PPO-Replay) is the baseline that fine-tunes the whole VLA, and the real-world Stage-1 uses SACfD. The numbers are correct.
evidence: Section IV freezes the VLM during action-head RL; PPO-Replay is the baseline and real-robot RL uses SACfD. Table I gives MetaWorld unseen-10 success 0.51/0.39/0.80.
applied_changes: {"one_line": "Alternates online RL on an action head over a frozen VLM with full-model SFT on expert demos and RL successes. MetaWorld unseen-10 success: 0.51 SFT / 0.39 PPO-Replay / 0.80 iRe-VLA."}

The 'short' field holds the full title instead of the method name.
evidence: Primary abstract and method distinguish binary loss weighting of diffusion behavior model from separate TD3+BC actor regularization.
applied_changes: {"short": "DIVO", "family": "generalrl", "one_line": "DIVO (IROS 2025): trains a diffusion behavior model with binary advantage-based loss weights, then regularizes a TD3+BC actor toward diffusion samples with non-negative advantage; reports gains on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze."}

label: Table tennis BGS

label: HG-DAgger
original_allegation: Mixes simulation and real-car results. label: DAgger

applied_changes: {"one_line": "Action-conditioned model scores hallucination per imagined chunk (AUROC 0.9375 on 50 human-labeled LIBERO chunks); scores down-weight chunk rewards in GRPO. LIBERO Spatial/Goal/Object average 63.7 vs 60.9 for reproduced WoVR* (no PACE)."}

label: FIPER
original_allegation: Tone. The one_line contains the phrase 'MAJOR CORRECTION:', which looks like an internal audit note that leaked into public text. It also suggests the authors misreported their results, but the paper discloses this itself. The numbers are correct. The code link works but redirects: utiasDSL/fiper now points to learnsyslab/fiper.
evidence: Primary paper discusses time-varying versus conformal thresholds and corresponding false-alarm limitations; removed internal MAJOR CORRECTION label without weakening that caveat.
applied_changes: {"one_line": "Failure detection combines RND out-of-distribution scores with action-chunk entropy, calibrated on successes. Time-varying thresholds achieve accuracy 0.78 and TWA 0.65; the CP-band variant with a false-alarm bound achieves TWA 0.62."}

label: GSWorld
original_allegation: Mixes up sim and real. 'Real DAgger at iteration 5' reads as if the DAgger corrections came from real robot data. In the paper, the corrective data is generated in simulation (a motion planner in GSWorld) and the policy is only evaluated on the real FR3. The numbers themselves are correct, and the 8-cell sim-underestimates-real claim checks out (Table I).
evidence: Method collects corrections with motion planning after resetting simulation to pre-failure states. Appendix Table II evaluates sim-trained DAgger on real FR3: iteration-5 four-task mean 63.75 versus 55 from scratch. Table I: sim below real in all eight cells.
applied_changes: {"one_line": "3DGS plus ManiSkill3 photoreal twin for evaluation and DAgger. Sim underestimates real in all 8 ACT/pi0 cells. Sim-collected DAgger, evaluated on the real FR3: 63.75% vs 55% training from scratch at iteration 5 (4-task average)."}

label: Self-Improving Loops for Visual Robotic Planning (SILVR)
original_allegation: (a) The one_line overstates the default setup. In the main method, rollouts are filtered by a sparse success signal (ground truth in the main experiments), and the initial in-domain model is trained on expert demos. 'Without human rewards or expert demos' only holds in separate ablations (a VLM judge as the filter; suboptimal initial data), and without any filtering the MetaWorld gains were only marginal. The one_line also leaves out a key part of the mechanism: optional composition with an internet-pretrained video model (IPA). (b) The code field points to the project page, not the code; the project page links github.com/brown-palm/silvr, which holds the code. (c) The short field is the full title; every other entry uses the acronym. (Note: the v1 title was 'Self-Adapting Improvement Loops for Robotic Learning'. The current title is correct.)
evidence: Algorithm 1 filters rollouts by sparse success; section 3.3 optionally composes an internet-video prior. VLM filtering/suboptimal initial data are separate ablations. No-filter MetaWorld gains are marginal. Linked brown-palm/silvr repository verified HTTP 200.
applied_changes: {"short": "SILVR", "code": "https://github.com/brown-palm/silvr", "one_line": "Video-generative planner (optionally composed with an internet-pretrained video model) iteratively fine-tuned on its own success-filtered rollouts; improves over iterations on unseen MetaWorld and two real-arm tasks, and still improves with VLM-judged filtering or suboptimal initial data (ICLR 2026)."}

label: DiWA

Everything else is correct: close-drawer 59.14 → 91.95, no physical interaction during fine-tuning, a frozen DreamerV2-style RSSM trained on play data, and Freiburg/UTN affiliations.
evidence: Table 1 maximum CALVIN gain is 77.01−35.63=41.38 points; close-drawer 59.14 to 91.95. Zero physical interactions during adaptation. Rounded range changed to 17–41 and simulation setting labeled.
applied_changes: {"one_line": "DPPO inside a frozen RSSM trained on play data, with no physical interaction during fine-tuning. CALVIN simulation skills gain roughly 17-41 points over the base policy (close-drawer 59.14% to 91.95%)."}

id: EBRL: Asynchronous Embodied RL by Multi-Grained Resource Management
label: EBRL: Asynchronous Embodied RL by Multi-Grained Resource Management
original_allegation: The 2.5x convergence number is presented as 'versus prior systems'. label: PureJaxRL
original_allegation: The speedups leave out their setting, and the 1000x baseline is stated more loosely than in the source. The README gives 10x over CleanRL's PyTorch PPO without vectorization, on CartPole and MinAtar-Breakout. label: SimDist
original_allegation: The headline result is overclaimed and pairs the wrong data budget with it. (a) 'Quadruped 5/5 where RLPD and IQL fail': SimDist got 5/5 in only 5 of 6 speed settings (4/5 on Slippery Slope at 0.1 m/s). IQL did not fail on Foam (1/5, 2/5, 3/5), and RLPD has no Foam result because it destabilized the robot. (b) The '15-30 min' figure comes from the paper's contribution list, but the quadruped results it is paired with used 32.1 min (Foam) and 35.7 min (Slippery Slope) of real data.

applied_changes: {"one_line": "Pretrain a latent world model in simulation; freeze encoder, reward and value, adapt dynamics on real data and plan with MPPI. Go2 slippery slope: 14/15 successes across three speeds after 35.7 minutes, versus IQL/RLPD 0/15."}

label: RoboEvolve
original_allegation: (1) The org field is malformed ('Ying-Cong Chen group, per author list)' has a stray parenthesis and reads like an internal note), although the arXiv HTML clearly lists the affiliations.
